How it was scored

  • Scanned with OpenSCAP in the image build on 2026-10-21 04:24 UTC.
  • Content: SCAP Security Guide 0.1.82, profile “Canonical Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) V1R5” (xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_stig), as published.
  • Score = rules passed ÷ (rules passed + rules failed). Every rule listed under Exemptions failed in the scan and counts as a failure in the score. Not-applicable and not-checked rules are not scored.
  • The build's OpenSCAP gate was enforced: floor 90%, and no failing rule without a documented exemption.
  • FIPS mode is enabled, using the OS vendor's FIPS cryptographic modules.
  • No Ubuntu Pro subscription is included. Ongoing ESM and FIPS updates require your own Ubuntu Pro subscription.

An OpenSCAP score measures this image against SSG content. It is not a certification, authorization or accreditation, and it is not an assessment of your system.

Exemptions (14)

Each rule below fails in the image for the reason given, and the last column is what you do to meet it on your instance. The reasons and actions come from the build record (the signed POA&M lists the same rules).

RuleSTIG IDCategoryWhy it fails in the imageWhat you do
grub2_password
Set Boot Loader Password in grub2		UBTU-24-102000AWS Marketplace policy: you complete it after launchAWS Marketplace policy prohibits meeting this rule in an AMI: "AMI must not contain hardcoded secrets such as system user and service passwords (including hashed passwords)" and "Password-based authentication for instance services is prohibited. This applies even if the password is generated, reset, or defined by the user at launch"; Linux AMIs "must allow users to get fully privileged access (for example, to allow sudo access)" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/product-and-ami-policies.html). The rule needs a boot loader or root password hash in the image, or a sudo password for the key-only default user.After launch run sudo stigready-set-credentials (installed in the image): it sets your own GRUB superuser and password, root password and a sudo password for your admin user, and removes NOPASSWD, which meets this rule on your instance.

package_opensc_installed
Install the opensc Package For Multifactor Authentication		UBTU-24-100900Smart card / CAC: needs your PKISmart card (CAC/PIV) login needs a card reader and the customer's own PKI: their CA certificates, OCSP/CRL endpoints and certificate-to-user mapping. A cloud instance has no reader, and no CA or mapping we could ship is correct for any customer. Some of these rules only install or enable a package; they are exempt with the class so the image does not run a smart card stack that cannot be used, and the customer enables it with their PKI.If you use CAC/PIV: install opensc and pcsc-lite, enable pcscd, install your CA bundle, and configure SSSD (or pam_pkcs11 on Ubuntu) certificate verification, OCSP/CRL and the certificate mapping for your directory.
